chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from one of his companions, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam, who said:

I was present at the Sacred House (Kaaba), and a man was calling out to Abu Ja'far al-Mansur while he was circumambulating, saying: 'O Commander of the Faithful! These two men came to my brother at night and took him out of his house, and he has not returned to me. By Allah, I do not know what they did with him.' So he said to them, 'What did you do with him?' They said, 'O Commander of the Faithful, we spoke to him and he returned to his house.' So he said to them, 'Meet me tomorrow after the Asr prayer in this place.'

So they met him the next day after the Asr prayer, and I was present. He said to Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him), while holding his hand, 'O Ja'far, judge between them.' He said, 'O Commander of the Faithful, you judge between them.' He said to him, 'By my right upon you, you must judge between them.'

So Ja'far (peace be upon him) came out, and a reed prayer mat was spread for him, and he sat on it. Then the disputants came and sat before him. He said, 'What are you saying?' He said, 'O Son of the Messenger of Allah, these two came to my brother at night and took him out of his house. By Allah, he has not returned to me, and by Allah, I do not know what they did with him.' He said, 'What do you two say?' They said, 'O Son of the Messenger of Allah, we spoke to him, then he returned to his house.'

So Ja'far (peace be upon him) said, 'O scribe, write: In the Name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever comes to a man at night and takes him out of his house, he is responsible for him, unless he establishes proof that he returned him to his house.' O scribe, remove this one and strike his neck.'

He said, 'O Son of the Messenger of Allah, by Allah, I did not kill him, but I restrained him. Then this one came and ambushed him and killed him.' He said, 'I am the Son of the Messenger of Allah. O scribe, remove this one and strike the neck of the other.'

He said, 'O Son of the Messenger of Allah, by Allah, I did not torment him, but I killed him with one strike.' So he ordered his brother to strike the first man's neck. Then he ordered the other one, so they struck his sides, imprisoned him, and wrote on his head: 'He shall be held for life and whipped fifty lashes every year.'

key_terms.أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful, a title used for the Caliph (Abu Ja'far al-Mansur) in this narrative.
key_terms.جَنْبَيْهِ: His sides, referring to the specific corporal punishment administered.
key_terms.ضَامِنٌ: Responsible/Guarantor, indicating legal liability for the person taken out.
key_terms.طَرَقَ: To knock upon or visit suddenly, specifically used here for coming to a house at night.
key_terms.يُحْبَسُ عُمُرَهُ: He shall be held for life, indicating a life sentence in prison.

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on liability when two people take someone out of their home at night and one kills him?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the principle of *al-daman* (liability) in Shia jurisprudence, where Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) applies the Prophetic precedent that removing someone from their home at night makes one responsible for their life unless proven otherwise. The narrative highlights the distinction between *qatl bi'l-mithl* (retaliatory killing) for the direct killer and *diyya* (blood money) with imprisonment for the one who restrained the victim, demonstrating the nuanced application of justice in cases of joint causation.
